newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS- FEB 24.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS- FEB 24.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek general press:

--The disagreement between government and teachers over how much newly-appointed teachers actually make is no longer a reason for the six-week strike to continue, Education Minister Gerasimos Arsenis and Deputy Finance Minister Nikos Christodoulakis said last night. But teachers have said they will continue for a seventh week if their remaining demands are not met.

--Tactical manoeuvres by conservative opposition New Democracy party leader Miltiades Evert and ND deputy Costas Karamanlis, who has been put forward as an alternative for party leader by some 30 deputies, led to nothing over the weekend despite backstage efforts from both sides to get the other to withdraw.
--Two-thirds (and almost all dissenters) were absent from decision-making ruling party PASOK meetings over the weekend.

--Recent measures to combat Athens' notorious air pollution - including catalytic converters on cars and stringent checks on fuel emissions - have brought smog levels down by 25 percent over the last five years, experts say.

--A former anti-terrorism expert at the public order ministry was the target of yesterday's abortive bomb attack by the shadowy Resistance Fighting Front. The one-kilogram dynamite bomb had been placed at the woman's door.

--PASOK is "clinically dead", following the absence of 100 members of the Central Committee from its meeting over the weekend. Environment Minister Costas Laliotis proposed starting anew rather than restructuring "only half of PASOK".

--Plans to abolish entrance examinations for universities are moving ahead, with Education Minister Gerasimos Arsenis saying that students entering senior high school this year will be the first to benefit from the new system. --Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
